name: print.boot
title: Print a summary of a bootstrap object

origin.description: Print the simulation type, the call, and the original value, bias, and standard error of each bootstrap statistic.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A bootstrap object from boot, censboot, tilt.boot, or tsboot.

arguments.name: digits
arguments.text: Significant digits used to print the summary. The default is getOption("digits"), usually 7.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based positions of the statistics to summarize. The default is every column of t.
Further arguments passed to or from other methods.

origin.details: Bias is the mean of the replicates minus the original value. The standard error is the square root of the sample variance, with missing replicates removed. If the call supplied importance weights, the ratio importance-sampling moments are printed instead, together with the plain mean of the replicates. A column that is entirely missing is reported as a warning rather than a row of the table.
origin.value: The bootstrap object, invisibly. The summary is printed.
origin.example:
set.seed(1)
stat <- function(d, i) mean(d[i])
print(boot(1:10, stat, R = 50))

translation.description: Print the simulation type, the call, and the original value, bias, and standard error of each bootstrap statistic.

arguments.name: digits
arguments.text: Significant digits for the summary. The default 7 matches R's digits option.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based positions to summarize. None means every column of t.

translation.details: Bias is the mean of the finite replicates minus the original value. The standard error uses the sample variance with divisor n - 1. The heading depends on sim and on whether the call supplied strata or importance weights. The same text is returned.
translation.example:
from boot.resample import boot, print_boot
from boot.rng import set_seed
import numpy as np

def stat(d, i):
    i = np.asarray(i, dtype=int)
    return float(np.mean(np.asarray(d)[i - 1]))

set_seed(1)
print_boot(boot(np.arange(1, 11), stat, R=50))
